name: Nadiral-Esker
description: Rolling continents break around shallow seas, their interiors scored by bioluminescent seas. Beyond towering mountain ranges, the land runs to a horizon that feels hand-drawn.
Storm season reorganizes all plans. When the pressure falls, animals go quiet, instruments drift, and the horizon turns the color of an old wound.
Geologists argue about the strata here: several layers appear deposited out of order, as if the planet's history were shuffled like cards.
The charts mark this world in cautious amber. Those who ignore the marking tend to come back rich, changed, or not at all.
